description: A hand-selected 3-waypoint Mars sol plan (real Jezero DEM, assets/mars/) whose final leg threads within one grid cell of a real ~19.7deg slope cell (445,431) that sits almost exactly on the spawn->goal straight line (perpendicular offset ~0m, so the detour cost stays near zero, unlike a lateral detour which reliably stalls the mission's 75s no-progress clock - see tools/find_mars_mixed_plan_fixture.mjs for how this was found and why). At DEFAULT_GUARDRAILS (maxSlopeDeg 25) the co-pilot's plan-time hazard check passes it clean (19.7 < 25); the ensemble then splits between 'arrived' and 'stalled' purely from DRIFT_PCT's seeded localization drift pushing the believed-vs-true steering off enough, on some seeds, to lose the last ~220m approach. At a tighter guardrail (maxSlopeDeg <= 19) the SAME cell is flagged as a plan-time hazard and the run holds before ever driving, on every seed (planning is deterministic, independent of drift/seed).

measured.note: Measured this session (node, real assets/mars DEM) so the numbers below are verifiable, not asserted from memory. See tests/sol-sim.test.mjs and tests/ensemble.test.mjs for the exact reproductions.
measured.tippedTradeoffBlocked: The real Mars DEM has zero cells >= the rover's fixed 32deg physical tip limit within ~8.3km of spawn (nearest is (271,852) at 32.17deg, 8335m from spawn / 9006m from goal), and mission.js's STALL_TIMEOUT_S=75s caps any sustained move-away-from-goal excursion at roughly 225m (75s * 3 m/s) before the run is forced to 'stalled'. No sol plan can both stay within that stall grace and reach a >=32deg cell, so 'tipped' cannot be produced near this goal by any guardrail/drift combination without changing DRIFT_PCT (forbidden) or terrain/mission logic (out of this lane's file ownership). Acceptance (4)'s loose-vs-mid TIPPED comparison is therefore BLOCKED on the shipped DEM; the HELD half of the same comparison (tight vs mid) is implemented and green.
